rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis proposes an ALD-deposited alumina coating, whereas the target uses a DC magnetron-sputtered AlTiCrZrNbTa refractory high-entropy alloy coating with varied Al content. These are fundamentally different kinds of interventions (a binary oxide coating vs. a multi-principal-element alloy coating), so the intervention type does not match.
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis specifies high-temperature oxidation at 1200–1500 °C in an oxidizing atmosphere, while the target uses isothermal oxidation in flowing steam at 1000 °C and 1100 °C. The temperature ranges and atmospheres (steam vs. unspecified oxidizing atmosphere) differ substantially, placing them in different regimes.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis invokes a simple physical barrier mechanism via a dense alumina layer. The target's mechanism involves preferential nucleation of Al2O3, TiO2, and Cr2O3 forming a composite oxide layer, with excess Al causing detrimental intermetallic formation and oxide discontinuity. These are different mechanistic classes (simple barrier vs. complex selective oxidation and intermetallic disruption).
rationale.outcome_agreement: The hypothesis predicts a 30–50% reduction in oxide scale growth rate for the coated cladding vs. uncoated. The target predicts and demonstrates a non-monotonic effect of Al content on oxidation rate, with an optimum at ~10 at.% Al and worse performance at higher Al contents, measured by mass gain and oxygen penetration. The predicted property (oxidation rate reduction) and the nature of the comparison (coated vs. uncoated baseline) differ from the target's comparison among alloy compositions.
